cards.diagnostics: Diagnostics are provenance-tagged via the optional `source` field (naming the producing tool/linter) and `codeDescription.href` (linking to external documentation for the code), and can carry opaque `data` that round-trips into a later textDocument/codeAction request so the client can offer targeted quick-fixes tied to a specific diagnostic instance.
guarantees: publishDiagnostics is a one-way notification (not a request/response), meaning there is no server-side acknowledgment built into the protocol message itself.
The pull model's resultId mechanism is intended to let servers signal 'nothing changed' cheaply instead of re-transmitting a full diagnostic list on every pull.
cards.implementation_paths_and_technique: Two complementary protocol mechanisms: an unsolicited push notification (publishDiagnostics) for server-driven updates, and a request/response pull protocol (textDocument/diagnostic) with a resultId-based caching/unchanged-report optimization to avoid re-sending identical diagnostic sets.
cards.method: The Diagnostic interface carries: range (span), an optional severity (DiagnosticSeverity: Error=1, Warning=2, Information=3, Hint=4), an optional code (integer or string) with an optional codeDescription (an href to more documentation, added 3.16), an optional source string naming the producing tool (e.g. 'typescript'), a message, optional tags (DiagnosticTag: Unnecessary=1, Deprecated=2, added 3.15), optional relatedInformation (an array of related locations elsewhere in the workspace), and optional data (opaque payload preserved between publishDiagnostics and a later codeAction request, added 3.16). Two delivery models exist: (1) textDocument/publishDiagnostics, a server-to-client notification that replaces the previously published diagnostic set for a given document/version wholesale; (2) textDocument/diagnostic (the 'pull' model, added in 3.17), a client-initiated request in which the server can return a resultId for a diagnostic report set, and on a subsequent pull the server may return an 'unchanged' report referencing that resultId instead of re-sending full diagnostics, letting the client reuse its previously cached result.

cards.method: Koka's type system assigns every function an effect row (a set of effect labels, polymorphic via row variables) in addition to its value type. The compiler (implemented in Haskell) lowers effect handlers using an evidence-passing translation, refined in the ICFP'21 paper into a monadic translation into plain lambda calculus for efficient compilation, with a dedicated C backend; it also supports a JavaScript backend and an in-progress WASM (Emscripten) backend. cards.method: Starting from a functional core language with explicit control flow, the Perceus algorithm emits precise reference-count increment/decrement (dup/drop) instructions such that, for cycle-free data, no live object is ever collected and no dead object is ever retained ('garbage-free'). cards.problem: Compiling Rust requires managing a very large, cyclically-referential graph of type and IR data with acceptable memory/time overhead, and re-running the whole compiler on every edit is too slow, so rustc needs cheap allocation, fast type-equality, and a way to reuse previous work.

reusable_methods.concern: Allocation and deallocation cost for the millions of short-lived IR/type/AST nodes a compiler front end creates in one run
counterexamples: Does not transfer to a long-lived interactive process: rust-analyzer's syntax layer is documented as reference-counted structurally shared green nodes (ref_count field in the node header, children held as Arc), not a bump arena freed in bulk, because an editor session never reaches a point where everything can be dropped at once (web: rust-analyzer syntax page).

rustc's own DroplessArena restriction is a counterexample inside the method: the technique buys allocation speed by giving up destructors, so any data needing Drop is pushed back onto the ordinary allocator (rustc-core.rustc.c04).

Bulk-free forfeits early reclamation: arena data in rustc is explicitly not deallocatable before compilation ends (rustc-core.rustc.c03), so peak memory is bounded by total allocation, not by live set.

reusable_methods.concern: Allocation and deallocation cost for the millions of short-lived IR/type/AST nodes a compiler front end creates in one run
counterexamples: Does not transfer to a long-lived interactive process: rust-analyzer's syntax layer is documented as reference-counted structurally shared green nodes (ref_count field in the node header, children held as Arc), not a bump arena freed in bulk, because an editor session never reaches a point where everything can be dropped at once (web: rust-analyzer syntax page).

rustc's own DroplessArena restriction is a counterexample inside the method: the technique buys allocation speed by giving up destructors, so any data needing Drop is pushed back onto the ordinary allocator (rustc-core.rustc.c04).

Bulk-free forfeits early reclamation: arena data in rustc is explicitly not deallocatable before compilation ends (rustc-core.rustc.c03), so peak memory is bounded by total allocation, not by live set.

cards.problem: Provides an IDE-facing incremental analysis engine for Rust that must remain responsive and correct under continuous, partial edits, requiring lossless syntax trees and an incremental query architecture that avoids recomputing unrelated facts on every keystroke.

reusable_methods.concern: Recomputing unchanged derived facts on every invocation or every keystroke
counterexamples: Absent by design in Oxc: its fetched sources describe one-shot parser/transformer/linter/formatter tools with no query-caching or invalidation system, i.e. a batch tool can answer the 'don't redo work' problem with process-level re-execution plus a fast arena instead of a query graph (syntax-oxc.oxc card, query_caching_invalidation).
Absent in Rowan: the tree library deliberately provides no query layer, leaving incrementality to consumers (syntax-oxc.rowan card).
Not applicable to Perceus, which is a memory-management pass over generated code with no caching dimension (koka-effects.perceus data_oriented.query_caching_invalidation).
The claimed invalidation scope is unquantified: rust-analyzer's invariant is stated as a design property with no benchmark on actual recomputation scope (syntax-oxc.rust-analyzer.c04 uncertainty).

reusable_methods.project_baggage_to_reject: The IR must be sliced to the granularity you want to invalidate at: rust-analyzer's stated invariant that editing a function body does not invalidate global derived data implies a body-vs-signature split in the data model. rustc generates provider tables per crate; Salsa imposes the input/tracked/interned struct discipline on the whole program. Correctness of reuse rests on the dependency-tracking implementation, which none of the cards inspected in source.
reusable_methods.reusable_method: Express every derived fact as a pure function of explicitly recorded inputs, record the dependency edges as a by-product of execution rather than declaring them, and decide reuse at runtime by traversing recorded edges in recorded order.

reusable_methods.name: Diagnostics as accompanying data rather than as control flow
reusable_methods.project_baggage_to_reject: rust-analyzer's convention is a signature rule with nothing enforcing it; Salsa's exclusion from result equality is framework-provided but requires adopting the accumulator API; Oxc's channel model presumes a batch run with a terminating consumer. Note the internal tension: rust-analyzer's tuple return places diagnostics inside the value, which is the position Salsa's accumulator design deliberately avoids.
reusable_methods.reusable_method: Make every analysis total — always return a value plus a diagnostic collection — and, where results are memoized, keep diagnostics on a channel that is explicitly excluded from result equality so error payloads cannot defeat identity-based short-circuiting.

reusable_methods.name: Green/red split: immutable position-free shared tree plus derived positioned cursor
reusable_methods.project_baggage_to_reject: Option-returning accessors propagate into every consumer of the typed AST; the red layer must be re-derived after edits; Rowan's docs.rs coverage was 19.05% at access time, so internals (exact refcount type, offset storage) are not confirmable from published docs; rust-analyzer's interner is currently per-file, limiting cross-file dedup. Round-trip losslessness is asserted in documentation with no enforcement mechanism identified in the fetched sources, hence the convention rung.
reusable_methods.reusable_method: Separate what the text is (immutable, position-free, dedupable, refcounted) from where it is (derived, cheap, discardable), and keep the derived layer out of any cache key; make the typed accessor layer total by returning Option rather than assuming grammar validity.

hidden_assumptions.statement: The corpus and all adoption-rung classifications silently assume this project is a Rust-implemented, long-lived, editor-facing semantic-analysis front end. This was inferred from the reference mix (rustc, salsa, rowan, rust-analyzer, oxc, miette, LSP) and never checked — the repository was never read and the boundary enum was empty. Every rung resting on lifetimes, privacy, newtypes, deny-lints, or must_use falls if the language premise is wrong; every rung resting on process shape (no abort-on-violation, input-proportional working set) falls if the project is a batch tool.

Query purity and result determinism are assumed achievable by convention: no Rust signature marks clock reads, iteration-order dependence, or ambient global access, yet memoization correctness, backdating, and deterministic simulation replay all silently presuppose exactly these properties. This is the same missing effect discipline the Koka cluster solves ex ante and Rust cannot express — the corpus's most load-bearing unstated premise.

hidden_assumptions.statement: Fetch-tool fidelity is assumed wherever a claim's uncertainty says 'summarizer-mediated': the corpus contains demonstrated fabrication (fluent Koka 'quotes' absent from the book source) and self-contradictory PDF extraction (Power of Ten rules oscillating between 'minimize' and 'prohibit' recursion). Quote-as-reported evidence is a distinct, weaker tier than read bytes, and no claim in the corpus reaches the read-bytes tier.

Guarantee scope conditions are assumed to hold silently at adoption time: Perceus's garbage-freedom assumes cycle-freedom (no cycle collector found); static allocation assumes startup-knowable maxima; result-identity short-circuiting assumes canonical, deterministic results; abort-on-violation assumes crashing is safe. None of these preconditions is checkable at any rung available to this project, so each adopted guarantee must be written with its scope attached or it will be repeated unscoped.

Provenance accounting is assumed complete because a query exists: the reduceBool incident shows that one unrecorded edge makes the assumption report read clean while wrong. Any adopted per-artifact assumption query inherits this failure mode for every opaque primitive — FFI calls, native evaluation, hand-admitted cached artifacts — and no rung catches it; only shrinking the opaque-primitive set does.

rejected_patterns.reason: Defeats backdating and result-identity short-circuiting: spans shift under every edit, so results never compare equal. At memoization boundaries diagnostics must ride an identity-excluded side channel (the Salsa accumulator shape); the tuple shape is acceptable only above or outside the query layer.
